topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its multidisciplinary audience, and the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer development through the accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation, three-dimensional tissue architecture, and cell culture models.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors: invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the differences between benign and malignant tumors through mechanisms of invasion and metastasis, histological progression, clinical risks, and standard nomenclature.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical and physiological mechanisms by which local tumor growth and metastatic dissemination cause patient illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine cancer frequency and mortality across human demographics and compare tumor patterns across diverse animal species as a feature of multicellularity.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, clinical applications, and limitations of population screening for cervical, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
